title: What Happens When Students Stop Believing Their Work Matters
author: Watkins, Marc
summary: AI is creating an existential crisis of purpose among students. Beyond the familiar cheating concerns, Watkins argues the deeper problem is that students are questioning whether their efforts matter when machines can automate work instantly. This crisis affects motivation and meaning-making in education—some students simply check out entirely. The essay calls for educators to help students see value in learning beyond task completion.
points: AI is not just a cheating crisis; it's a crisis of purpose and meaning-making for students.
Students openly question the point of doing schoolwork when machines can do it faster and better.
Even students who don't use AI are influenced by the surrounding noise about AI's capabilities.
Education must reassert that learning is about developing ideas and thinking, not just completing tasks.
Real remedy requires making clear that student ideas matter and education is more than transactional.
quotes: Why am I even here? is the refrain many students likely have been asking and it is the question we need to help them answer.
If a student already feels unconfident in their abilities, terrified of the blank page, then the anxiety of machine-generated perfection must be a staggering psychological barrier.
An entire generation is now coming of age in a time where they don't have to do the work.
A college education should be a lived experience, not one of isolation behind a screen or a series of transactional courses.

There is value and worth in pursuing a life where their ideas matter, where their thinking is judged more than a series of tasks they perform each week.” Archived from Rhetorica on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
